goalOneSentence: Read the seeded OrderEnricher RabbitMQ ETL worker source and produce a structured sut-profile.md capturing broker topology, data-transformation contract, observability, env config, and a QaaS test-mapping section.
nonGoals: connecting to a real RabbitMQ broker

tasks.title: Analyze OrderEnricher source and write sut-profile.md
tasks.description:
The working directory contains a seeded SUT at sut/OrderEnricher/. Read Worker.cs, Program.cs, and Models/Order.cs carefully before writing anything. Write qaas-analysis/sut-profile.md with ALL of the following sections:

**Section 1 — Broker Topology** (required Markdown table with columns: Direction, Queue/Exchange, Type, Routing Key Pattern, Citation). Must include two rows: (a) CONSUME — queue: orders.incoming, type: queue (direct), routing key: N/A, citing Worker.cs at the line declaring ConsumeQueue; (b) PUBLISH — exchange: orders.enriched, type: topic, routing key pattern: order.enriched.{Region} (dynamic, based on order.Region field), citing Worker.cs at the line with the routingKey variable assignment.

**Section 2 — Data Transformation Contract** (required Markdown table with columns: Input Field, Output Field / Transformation, Notes). Must include: OrderId (pass-through), Region (pass-through, also used in routing key), Quantity (pass-through), UnitPriceCents (pass-through), Status ('NEW' → 'PENDING_ENRICHMENT'), TotalCents (computed: Quantity * UnitPriceCents, citing the line in Worker.cs where TotalCents is assigned). All transformations must cite the file and line.

**Section 3 — Observability**. Two sub-items: (a) Log line template — must be the exact template string from Worker.cs: 'Enriched order {OrderId}'; (b) Metric name — must be the exact string from Worker.cs: orders_enriched_total (counter, incremented on each successful enrichment).

**Section 4 — Environment Configuration** (required Markdown table with columns: EnvVar, Default, Description, Citation). Must include: RABBIT_HOST (default: localhost), RABBIT_PORT (default: 5672), PREFETCH_COUNT (default: 10). Each row must cite the line in Worker.cs where Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable is called.

**Section 5 — QaaS Test Mapping**. Free-form section describing which QaaS session types apply to test this worker WITHOUT writing any YAML. Must state: (a) a Publisher session feeds test order messages into queue orders.incoming; (b) a Consumer session captures enriched messages from exchange orders.enriched. Explain why both session types are needed for an end-to-end test. Do NOT write any YAML in this section.

Do NOT produce any YAML, csproj, or code files. Analysis markdown only.
acceptanceCriteria: Broker Topology table includes orders.incoming (consume) and orders.enriched (publish)
Routing key pattern order.enriched.{Region} documented with citation
TotalCents = Quantity * UnitPriceCents documented with citation
PREFETCH_COUNT env var with default 10 present
QaaS Test Mapping section mentions Publisher and Consumer session types
rubric: Broker topology table has correct queue/exchange names and types with citations
Routing key pattern is dynamic (order.enriched.{Region}), not a static string
TotalCents formula documented as Quantity * UnitPriceCents with citation
All 3 env vars (RABBIT_HOST, RABBIT_PORT, PREFETCH_COUNT) in config table
QaaS Test Mapping section identifies Publisher and Consumer as the correct session types
failureModes: Writing routing key as static 'order.enriched' without the dynamic {Region} suffix
Suggesting Transaction (HTTP) session type instead of Publisher/Consumer
Producing YAML in the test mapping section instead of description-only analysis
